lesson: Administrative inference was treated as much stronger than the evidence supported. A late thematic switch without direct reporting should not justify an 82 percent forecast.
Filtering candidates through the actual starting lineup and their tactical roles worked well and preserved a solid positive score.
Low-observability identity questions require broader candidate discovery. The submitted names had little direct support and omitted the relevant Syrian campaigner.
Direct oral-argument evidence and correcting the candidate's full name supported appropriate concentration and a strong score.
Norway and the wider Nordic bloc need explicit coverage in forecasts about leadership of human-rights coalitions.
Direct reporting that identified the travel delegation justified very high concentration and nearly perfect scoring.
Polling and front-runner reporting correctly separated the two-candidate field and supported a useful degree of confidence.
Another starting midfield runner was omitted. Even for a set-piece-heavy side, preserve a slot for an active central midfielder beyond the main aerial targets.
